title: Proof-of-Workout Fraud Shield for Fitness Incentives
one_liner: A verification API that scores whether a gym visit or workout really happened, priced per verified event.
customer: Administrators of pay-per-visit fitness benefits (regional Medicare Advantage plans, employer stipend platforms), movement-reward and fitness-betting apps.
problem: Chain: Medicare Advantage plans are trimming fitness benefits (93 percent offered one in 2026 versus 95 percent in 2025, more cuts expected) and payers and employers shift toward pay-per-verified-visit and reward models (one employer wellness network lists over 20,000 employer partners), so money follows check-ins and step counts. Fraud (shared QR codes, spoofed steps, ghost visits, inflated gym counts) becomes the margin killer and nobody sells fraud scoring built for fitness.
solution: An SDK and API combining phone attestation, gym BLE or Wi-Fi beacons, wearable heart-rate and motion consistency, GPS and barometer, and device-sharing graphs into an authenticity score with an audit trail, ring detection and a dispute workflow for gyms.
why_now: Benefit cuts push payers to pay-per-use, wearable aggregator APIs make cross-signal checks cheap, and mobile attestation is mature; HIPRA-style consent rules make audit trails a requirement.
revenue_model: $0.05-0.20 per verified event with a $2-5k monthly minimum, plus a gain share on recovered fraud.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is a labeled fraud dataset: once you process millions of visits you can sell audits to payers, and because you are neutral infrastructure you compete with no wearable or gym software vendor.
first_30_days: Find 2-3 reward or betting apps or one regional benefit administrator, run their last 90 days of check-ins through a prototype scorer, quantify suspected fraud, and charge $5-10k for the audit before integrating.

title: AI Shuttle Mediation for Estranged Families
one_liner: Each estranged party talks privately with an AI that drafts consensus 'bridge' statements and safe first-contact messages, leading to a human-mediated reunion within six weeks.
customer: Estranged adult children and parents (about a quarter of US adults report estrangement from a relative), paying $300-600 per participant, plus elder-law firms and hospital social workers paying $1-3k per reconnection case.
problem: Estrangement is common, painful and costly (unrepresented elders, contested estates), and the first contact is where reconciliation dies because neither side wants to go first. Coaches cost $150 an hour or more, and both parties rarely agree to therapy together.
solution: A structured program. A safety screen excludes abuse cases. Each party completes private AI-guided sessions to articulate needs and non-negotiables. A consensus engine produces candidate bridge statements that both sides rate independently. The first-contact letter or call is scripted and rehearsed in role-play. It ends with a human-mediated 90-minute conversation.
why_now: DeepMind's 2024 'Habermas Machine' showed LLM mediators can find statements groups prefer over human mediators. 2026 voice models handle emotionally sensitive role-play. Estrangement is now widely discussed, and aging and estate systems increasingly hit its costs.
revenue_model: Per-party program fee, B2B per-case fees from elder-law firms and hospitals, and success bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Reconciliation fails on asymmetric readiness: one side is ready and the other is not. An AI that can shuttle privately with each side at zero social cost solves 'who goes first', which is the real blocker.
first_30_days: Partner with two family-therapist mediators. Recruit 20 pilot participants from estrangement support communities at $300 each. Measure first-contact and second-conversation rates, then approach five elder-law firms with the results.

title: Time-to-First-Part: Install Readiness for Machine Dealers
one_liner: A pre-delivery site-scan and commissioning package that gets backlogged machines cutting parts weeks sooner.
customer: Machine-tool, laser and robot dealers and OEM sales teams, plus 20-200 employee manufacturers buying their first big machine.
problem: Unfilled capital-goods orders sit at $953B after a record $85.9B in July orders. Much of it lands in old buildings with no as-built drawings. Machines arrive to floors, doors, crane paths and utility drops that cannot take them, so crated $500k machines sit idle. Dealers often get paid only at acceptance.
solution: A 20-minute phone or LiDAR walkthrough becomes an as-built model. Software checks the machine footprint, door and aisle clearance and rigging path, flags slab and vibration issues (with a ground-penetrating-radar partner), lists air, coolant and chip-handling needs, and produces a rigging plan and punch list. It can also dispatch vetted riggers and millwrights.
why_now: Reshoring is happening inside existing walls, the equipment backlog is at a record, and riggers and millwrights are scarce. Phone-based 3D capture (LiDAR, Gaussian splats) has matured.
revenue_model: $1.2-3k per site package, paid by the dealer or bundled into the machine price. 10-15% referral on rigging. Dealer team subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Dealers get paid at acceptance, so time-to-first-part is their cash-flow metric and they will pay to shorten it. The unfilled-order backlog hides a second backlog of installed-but-not-producing machines.
first_30_days: Sign three regional dealers (CNC, laser or robot) for a pilot. Do 10 scans with iPhones. Produce a sample report. Measure install days saved against comparable installs.

title: Carrier Watchtower: Insurer Failure Alerts for Lenders
one_liner: Early-warning scores on the thinly capitalized insurers behind mortgage collateral, sold to servicers before the next carrier failure.
customer: Mortgage subservicers, credit unions, community banks and MSR investors with Florida, Louisiana, California and Texas collateral.
problem: Insiders treat Florida as fixed because Citizens fell from 936K to about 395K policies. But take-out carriers got Citizens' data to cherry-pick policies. A CBS investigation (unverified detail) alleges owners of a receiving carrier diverted millions. Howden warns reinsurer returns may fall below cost of capital by 2027, so any reversal hits the retail layer first. If a carrier fails, thousands of loans lose hazard cover at once and servicers must force-place at multiples.
solution: Loan tape in, exposure out. Map each loan's insurer from insurance-tracking data to a live stress score built from statutory filings, reinsurance program renewals, assumed-policy concentration, complaint ratios, rating actions and regulator orders. Give a 90-day warning and a pre-negotiated replacement placement lane.
why_now: Florida's rapid depopulation of Citizens in 2025-26 moved risk onto newer, thinner balance sheets. Reinsurance is at record capital and softening now, and the margin squeeze is forecast for 2027.
revenue_model: SaaS priced at basis points or cents per loan per year, plus per-policy replacement placement fees.
non_obvious_insight: Analysts watch carrier surplus and lenders watch loans, but nobody joins the two. Rating agencies lag, and the soft market hides the fragility.
first_30_days: Build dossiers on the top 40 Florida carriers from public regulator filings. Sell a $5K exposure report to two credit unions or subservicers showing what share of their book sits with the weakest carriers.

title: Local-Law Radar for Data Center and Battery Developers
one_liner: A system that continuously reads city and county codes, planning agendas and minutes nationwide and warns developers which jurisdictions are drafting moratoria or new setback, noise and fire-safety rules before they pass.
customer: Land-acquisition and permitting teams at data-center, battery-storage, solar, EV-charging and peaker developers, siting consultants, and law-firm land-use groups.
problem: Local ordinances decide whether $100M-$1B projects get built, but roughly 19,000 municipalities publish codes and agendas as PDFs on inconsistent sites. Opposition-driven moratoria appear with weeks of notice, developers learn about them after buying land options, and existing zoning datasets capture setbacks and floor-area ratios, not conditional-use or moratorium rules for new infrastructure types.
solution: A scraper and LLM pipeline over municipal-code hosts and agenda platforms (Legistar, CivicClerk, PrimeGov and similar) that classifies items by project type, alerts on early signals ('first reading', 'study session', 'interim urgency ordinance'), answers 'is X permitted at parcel Y and under what conditions?', and scores county risk. Two land-use paralegals curate the output.
why_now: Data-center and battery-storage siting fights surged through 2025-26, including after the Jan 2025 Moss Landing battery fire (background, verify), and LLMs can now read messy municipal PDFs cheaply enough to cover thousands of jurisdictions.
revenue_model: $2-10k/month per developer team, $60-250k/year enterprise plans, and $500-2,000 per-parcel reports.
non_obvious_insight: Moratoria are telegraphed weeks ahead in public agendas that nobody reads at scale, so the value is the leading indicator, not the code text. A stranded land option costs far more than the subscription.
first_30_days: Cover the three states with the most data-center activity and track about 500 jurisdictions' agendas. Publish a weekly free moratorium tracker, sell five developers or site-selection consultants at $2.5k/month, and back-test which past moratoria would have been flagged 30 days early.

title: Chute-Side Cow Counts for Ag Lenders
one_liner: Turn the vet's preg-check clipboard into a borrower-consented, third-party-verified herd inventory that banks can lend against.
customer: Community banks, Farm Credit associations and ag lenders with cattle loan books (they require it or pay per report, usually passed through to the borrower). Secondary payer is the cow-calf or heifer-development operator who wants bigger operating lines or bred-heifer financing on better terms.
problem: Cattle collateral has no VIN. Lenders verify with drive-by counts and borrower-supplied spreadsheets, and prosecutors in 2026 alleged a roughly $9.4M fraud that included a loan of $2.8M against 850 head. Farm loan delinquencies are rising while bred cows trade around $3,000+ per head, so a 500-cow borrower is $1.5M+ of collateral that nobody independent has counted.
solution: A 'Verified Herd Report' generated at the working day the vet is already doing. The vet or tech logs every head with an EID or visual tag scan (a $500 handheld reader plus a phone app), age class, pregnancy status and stage, and location. The vet e-signs and the borrower approves sharing with one tap. The lender gets a portal with timestamped, geotagged counts and year-over-year flags (head count down, pregnancy rate down, tags not matching last year). A second light pass happens at weaning. The vet earns a per-head fee for data they already write down and throw in the truck door pocket.
why_now: Federal EID ear tags became mandatory for many interstate cattle movements in Nov 2024, so per-head digital ID is now normal and cheap. Herd rebuilding at record cattle prices is being financed with debt, lenders entered 2026 carrying operating losses from 2023-2025 (rising delinquencies and restructures), and a fresh cattle-collateral fraud case is making ag loan committees ask for verification. Fall preg-check season is running right now (Sept-Nov).
revenue_model: $2-3 per head per verification, split roughly 50/50 with the vet practice, charged to the borrower or the lender as a loan condition. Add a portfolio dashboard for lenders at $500-2,000 per month once an institution has 100+ verified borrowers. Later, sell the verified inventory and pregnancy data to lenders as an underwriting input (advance rates on verified bred heifers).
non_obvious_insight: The vet is the only independent professional who physically handles every animal in the herd once or twice a year. They count, tag-check and pregnancy-check every cow, and that data dies on a clipboard. Vets refuse to police clients, but they will happily attest to what they handled when the borrower initiates the request, so the conflict-of-interest problem disappears. Honest borrowers are the real buyers: verified bred females can justify higher advance rates, and that cheap capital funds the fee many times over.
first_30_days: Preg-check season is live, so sign up 3 rural practices that each do several thousand head of fall preg-checks. Pitch 3-4 community-bank ag lenders (target the one who has been burned by a herd count before; work through state bankers' association ag committees). Run a pilot on about 10 willing borrowers with a form-based app and a PDF report, charging $2/head. Gather a before and after on what the lender learned that the drive-by inspection missed, then use that to sell the annual program.

title: RoboManual: Appliance Manuals Written for Humanoids
one_liner: A licensed library of articulated digital twins and operating procedures (where to press, how the latch moves, how much force) for the 500 most common home appliances, sold to home-robot makers and to appliance brands that want their products to be robot-ready.
customer: Home and general-purpose robot companies and robot foundation-model labs (1X, Figure, Sunday-type startups, Tesla-adjacent teams, lab groups training manipulation policies). Later, appliance OEMs (dishwashers, washers, ovens, fridges) and retailers.
problem: Home humanoids ship into thousands of models of dishwashers, washers, ovens and jars. 1X's Neo, the first humanoid actually delivered to consumers, leans on remote human operators for tasks like laundry and dishes because robots do not know how to operate your specific machine. Appliance makers wrote manuals for humans; nobody owns the equivalent for machines: hinge axes, latch travel, button actuation force, timing and failure modes.
solution: A physical-measurement studio that scans and instruments appliances. It produces articulated 3D assets (URDF/USD) with annotated affordances (press points, required force, latch and door kinematics, common jams) plus step-by-step procedure graphs and video of human demonstrations. Delivered as a dataset license and a lookup API keyed by model number, so a robot can scan a label and retrieve its operating plan. Every deployed robot's failures feed back to update the manual. Appliance OEMs pay for inclusion and a 'robot-graspable' certification.
why_now: Consumer humanoids started shipping in 2026 (1X Neo, $20k or $499/month) and are teleop-assisted, so every learned procedure has a direct dollar value in removed operator hours. Sim-based training pipelines are hungry for articulated real-world assets. Industrial pilots by Figure, Agility and Apptronik make robot makers seek reusable object knowledge.
revenue_model: Dataset licenses of $25-100k per year per lab or robot maker, per-lookup API fees at scale, OEM inclusion and certification fees ($20-50k per product line), and custom scan projects.
non_obvious_insight: Robots do not lack general knowledge about 'a dishwasher'. They lack knowledge about this latch and this button lag. The moat is physical measurement labor plus fleet feedback, not AI, so big labs will not bother to build it early. It is the 'second manual' of the appliance industry.
first_30_days: Partner with a scratch-and-dent appliance outlet and a repair shop for scan access. Capture 50-100 top-selling dishwashers, washers, dryers, microwaves and ovens with photogrammetry, a force gauge and video of human operation. Produce cleaned articulated assets with affordance labels and sell a pilot pack to 2-3 home-robot startups at $25-50k.

title: Assisted Short Sales for Underwater Auto Loans
one_liner: Record auto originations lead to record delinquencies and a repossession glut. Give lenders a mortgage-style short sale for cars that recovers more than auction does.
customer: Credit unions and subprime and indirect auto lenders with rising 60-plus-day delinquencies.
problem: Auto originations hit a record $211B and auto delinquencies also hit a record (CNBC and others, Aug 2026). Lenders' only tool at scale is repossession and auction, which is slow, costly and yields discounted recoveries. Borrowers keep a deficiency balance and wrecked credit, and lenders lose more than a cooperative sale would cost them.
solution: At 45-60 days delinquent, the lender offers the borrower a lender-blessed voluntary sale. The platform lists the car at retail to dealers and private buyers, handles payoff letters, title and lien release in each state, and converts the shortfall into a small structured note or forgiveness within lender-set limits. The lender pays only when its net recovery beats projected repo loss.
why_now: Delinquencies at records, auction supply pressure, and credit unions with growing delinquent books and a reputation to protect. Mortgage short-sale playbooks are well understood, but nobody has ported them to autos.
revenue_model: Flat fee (about $500-$700) or 3-5% of sale price per completed sale, plus a performance share of recovery improvement over projected repo loss.
non_obvious_insight: Lenders already lose money on repossession, but their servicing, collections and legal workflows are built around it, so no infrastructure exists to choreograph title, payoff and buyer across 50 states. The product is that plumbing.
first_30_days: Partner with two or three credit unions with 5k-plus delinquent auto loans. Run a manual pilot in one state with a small dealer buyer network, comparing net recovery per unit against actual auction results. Use the data to sign a master services agreement.

title: PFAS Test-Result Exchange for Small Brands
one_liner: A members' data pool where small brands share lab results indexed by supplier, material lot and SKU, so nobody pays $500+ to test the same fabric or coating twice.
customer: Product-compliance managers at small and mid-size apparel, outdoor, cookware, cosmetics, textile and food-packaging brands and importers ($5M-$200M revenue) selling into US states with PFAS product laws and into the EU.
problem: PFAS rules are fragmenting through state product bans and reporting laws, EU packaging limits and a pending EU universal restriction (all unverified in the briefing; re-check current status). Supplier declarations fail because suppliers often do not know what is in their coatings. Testing costs hundreds of dollars per sample, and small brands that buy from the same mills and coaters each test alone. 'PFAS-free' marketing claims also draw class actions.
solution: A neutral cooperative. Members upload lab PDFs, which are parsed automatically and tagged to supplier, mill, material spec and date. The exchange scores confidence per supplier-material ('3 independent labs, 12 samples, all under threshold'), flags outliers, recommends where a new test buys the most certainty per dollar, negotiates group lab rates, and generates the state or EU evidence file. Contributions earn credits.
why_now: State PFAS product deadlines and EU packaging PFAS limits are landing in 2025-26 (background, verify), total-fluorine screening is cheap enough to run routinely, and LLM parsing turns messy lab PDFs into structured data.
revenue_model: Membership of $3-15k/year by revenue tier, pay-per-query for non-contributors, a 10-15% margin on group lab testing, and a paid 'independently verified' badge program.
non_obvious_insight: Declarations fail through ignorance, not malice, so the durable defense is measurement. Measurement is a shared-cost, non-competitive good, like a credit bureau for materials. Antitrust risk is low if the pool holds test data only and never pricing.
first_30_days: Partner with one accredited lab and one trade association (outdoor or apparel). Recruit 10 founding members who contribute 200+ historical lab reports, stand up a spreadsheet-backed MVP with parsed PDFs, and charge a $2.5k founding fee.

title: Physically Verified Protocol Skills for Lab Agents
one_liner: A registry of agent-executable bench protocols where every version has actually been run on real instruments in independent labs, with signed control readouts, like CI badges backed by experiments.
customer: AI-native biotech startups, academic labs and core facilities running agent-directed workflows on liquid handlers (Opentrons OT-2/Flex, Hamilton, Tecan), plus cloud-lab operators. Buyers are lab managers and automation leads. Individual protocol authors are the supply side.
problem: Agent 'skills' registries are the new package supply chain (about 20% of the OpenClaw skill registry was reportedly malicious, and Okta paid about $200M for Permiso to sandbox skills). In biology a bad skill is not just a leaked token. It is a wasted week of bench time, a contaminated line, or a biosafety event. The last roughly 10% of manual steps in a 5,000-action workflow is tacit knowledge nobody writes down. Anthropic found that robotic automation fit ad hoc molecular-biology workflows poorly, and that expert review and bench work were the bottleneck rather than compute.
solution: Publish protocols as versioned skills: robot script, agent-readable instructions, parameter bounds, expected control values and hazard flags. A release counts as 'verified' only after it runs on at least 3 independent partner instruments and posts raw plate-reader or qPCR files with pass/fail on Z' and control CVs. Agents (or their human owners) can only pull skills above a reproducibility threshold. Static checks flag off-protocol reagent additions, unusual volumes or temperatures and dual-use red flags. Start with about 25 workhorse assays: Golden Gate/Gibson assembly, transformation, qPCR setup, viability, ELISA and Bradford.
why_now: The skills-as-supply-chain scare of 2026 and the Permiso acquisition prove buyers will pay to trust agent skills. Frontier labs and startups are now wiring agents to physical labs (Anthropic's wet lab, Medra, Lila, Transfyr's $25M seed to capture bench actions). Nobody sells verified physical execution, only software scanning.
revenue_model: Subscription per lab ($300-1,000/month for verified-skill access and update alerts); per-protocol certification fees paid by protocol authors and vendors ($1-3K per validation cycle); revenue share to partner validation labs; enterprise private registry for pharma automation groups.
non_obvious_insight: In software, tests are free, so registries compete on code. In biology the test is an experiment, so the moat is a network of physical validation sites and the accumulated failure data, not the code. Whoever owns the 'passes on real hardware' stamp owns trust in agentic bench work, and it also becomes the natural biosafety screen for skills.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 academic labs that already own OT-2s (they are common and often underused). Pick 10 protocols and run each 3 times per site. Publish the raw data and pass rates publicly as the marketing. Offer free verified skills to 30 labs via bioRxiv/Reddit/Slack communities, then charge $500/month for early access to new verified skills, alerts and private forks. Target 10 paying labs by month 3.

title: Widowhood Risk Program Sold to Medicare Payers
one_liner: Use hospice's early knowledge that a caregiver spouse is about to become a widow to enroll them in a 180-day protective program, paid for by Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans (especially those with dual-eligible special needs plans), ACOs and value-based primary care groups. Hospice agencies are the intake channel and receive a referral or administrative fee.
problem: The spouse of a hospice patient is the second patient, and nobody is paid to treat them. The caregiver spouse ran the pillbox, the checkbook, the driving and the meals. They have skipped their own appointments for months. In the weeks after the funeral their chronic conditions decompensate, and hospitalizations, ED visits and falls spike. The chaplain is the one person who sees the untouched pills, the empty refrigerator and the missed doctor visits. Payers only learn of the death through enrollment data that lags by weeks or months. Hospice bereavement services are a mailing program, and they do not bill for the spouse's medical risk.
solution: A two-part program. Before the death, a hospice chaplain or social worker flags a high-risk caregiver spouse using a 6-item checklist (medication management ownership, driving, isolation, own chronic conditions, missed visits) and refers them, with consent, to the program. After the death, a community health worker does a home visit within 72 hours, books a primary care appointment within 14 days, does a medication reconciliation, sets up meal delivery and transport, and runs structured check-ins at 2 weeks, 6 weeks and 6 months. The 6-week and 6-month checks include a prolonged grief screen (PG-13-R). Screen-positive people are referred to therapists trained in prolonged grief disorder treatment, billable to insurance because PGD has had its own diagnosis code (F43.81) since October 2022.
why_now: Medicare Advantage margins are under pressure, and plans are hunting for measurable avoidable-utilization programs and star-rating improvements. Value-based primary care and ACOs are expanding, and both are rewarded for preventing ED visits and admissions. Prolonged grief disorder became an official DSM-5-TR diagnosis in 2022, with an ICD-10-CM code from October 2022, so the treatment side is finally billable. Hospices are being asked to show quality beyond death itself. I could not verify current bereavement benefit designs at specific plans, so check that before pitching.
revenue_model: A per-enrolled-spouse fee of about $150 to $300 per month for 6 months, paid by the plan or ACO. This can convert to shared savings once there are a few hundred enrollees. Hospices receive a per-referral fee or a bereavement-outsourcing fee. Therapy referrals bill insurance directly, and the program can hold a small clinician panel. Employer benefit teams are a later channel.
non_obvious_insight: The highest-risk patient is not on the payer's radar and is not the patient the hospice is paid to look after. Only the hospice team knows the caregiver is fading, and it knows months before any claim or enrollment record does. The widowhood effect (well documented in the research literature, with elevated mortality and hospitalization in the months after a spouse dies) is an underpriced, predictable utilization event.
first_30_days: Pick one regional hospice and one value-based primary care group or small MA plan with a few thousand lives. Build the checklist and a simple spreadsheet workflow, then hire one community health worker or licensed social worker. Enroll the first 20 spouses at no charge, tracking ED visits, missed PCP visits and grief screens at 90 and 180 days. Use the data to sell a paid pilot to the plan or group before month 6. Get a HIPAA lawyer to sign off on the referral pathway and consent language.

title: Ship-Anywhere Prices for Pickup-Only Auction Lots
one_liner: Embed binding, lot-level delivered prices and a booked load-out window into online auction listings, so pickup-only machinery, estate and surplus lots attract national bidders, with the broker taking a cut of freight and the auctioneer sharing the hammer-price uplift.
customer: Regional auctioneers and liquidators selling machine tools, farm and construction equipment, restaurant and commercial surplus, estates and government surplus on HiBid, Proxibid, AuctionZip or their own sites. The buyer pays the freight.
problem: Pickup-only lots limit bidders to roughly a 100-200 mile radius and depress hammer prices. Existing help is an estimate (Proxibid embeds a uShip-based estimator showing approximate costs from comparable moves) or the buyer scrambling after winning, with a 3-7 day storage or removal deadline running. For a broker, pricing a 2,400-lb lathe at a rural site with one forklift and a Thursday-only load-out is a five-minute call. For a buyer it is a week of failed quotes, so out-of-area buyers simply do not bid.
solution: A listing-time tool. The auctioneer enters the pickup address and lot photos, dimensions and weight (a vision model plus a checklist estimates weight and cube from photos). It returns a binding delivered price by buyer ZIP, locked at bid time, including liftgate or loading, crating and a delivery window. On a win, it dispatches to a vetted pool of hot-shot, box truck, flatbed, lowboy and LTL carriers, books a load-out slot with the auction site's forklift operator, and pays carriers quickly. The auctioneer sees an A/B report of bidders per lot with and without delivered pricing.
why_now: Auction sales have moved largely online, and 2026 platform practice is to spell out freight and special-handling requirements and add approval steps before bidders commit to shipping charges. Vision models can now estimate weight and dimensions from listing photos well enough to quote. Small-load carriers (hot-shot, box truck) are plentiful because the freight market is soft and small carriers need loads.
revenue_model: 15-25% gross margin on freight, since small specialty loads carry higher broker margins than truckload. Typical freight ticket is $400-$1,800. Optionally share 5% of freight with the auctioneer, and later charge a per-lot fee tied to verified hammer-price uplift.
non_obvious_insight: The auctioneer's real problem is not shipping, it is bidder radius. Buyers do not bid on what they cannot price, so quote friction, not freight cost, kills out-of-area bids, which makes pre-bid freight pricing a hammer-price lever that can pay for itself. Also, the binding constraint at rural sites is the single forklift and a narrow load-out window, which no marketplace models. Solve that and carriers love the load because dwell is short.
first_30_days: Sign 5 auctioneers with many pickup-only lots. Concierge-price 50 lots by hand (form plus broker phone calls) and add a 'delivered to your ZIP' link in the lot description. Compare unique bidders and hammer price against matched control lots. Ship 40 lots under existing brokerage authority, and collect the freight margin only. Test estate sales and government surplus as second segments.

title: AI-Native Estate Settlement Firm Under Arizona ABS
one_liner: A licensed alternative business structure that runs uncontested probate and small-estate work end-to-end at a flat fee, with attorneys supervising agent-driven workflows.
customer: Families of decedents in Arizona with $100K-$2M estates (uncontested probates, small-estate affidavits, simple trust administration), referred by funeral homes, hospices, senior living communities and advisors.
problem: Hourly or percentage probate fees don't work for $300K estates, so many attorneys decline them. Families face 9-18 months (unverified estimate) and $5-20K bills, run by an overwhelmed executor.
solution: An Arizona ABS-licensed law firm using agent workflows for documents, court filings, creditor notices, asset inventory, accountings and distributions, with attorney supervision at ratios far above traditional practice. Fixed price ($2,900-$6,500) with a timeline guarantee, payable from the estate at closing, and one point of contact. Add-ons include real estate sale and tax return preparation.
why_now: Arizona has permitted non-lawyer ownership of law firms since 2021 and Utah runs a sandbox. LLMs are now reliable enough for supervised legal drafting, and Arizona has a large retiree population. The brief's estimate of $5T of yearly transfers is heavily weighted to the very wealthy, leaving middle-class estates unserved.
revenue_model: Flat fees plus ancillary margin on property sales, tax preparation and accounting.
non_obvious_insight: Hourly legal billing can't profitably serve middle-class estates, but a licensed software-first structure can undercut on price while earning better margins. The regulatory sandbox is both wedge and moat.
first_30_days: Apply for the ABS license or white-label under an existing ABS. Sign 3 funeral homes or senior communities for referrals. Run the first cases with a supervising attorney, and get counsel to review unauthorized-practice and fee-sharing rules.

title: Battery passport starter that feeds on repair-shop events
one_liner: A cheap battery-passport package for e-bike and small pack makers, plus a repair-shop scanning app that supplies the lifecycle events the passport is legally supposed to track.
customer: Small and mid-size European e-bike, e-scooter and cargo-bike brands, pack assemblers, and industrial or storage battery integrators above 2 kWh. The battery passport must exist from 18 Feb 2027. Independent repair shops and refurbishers are the second user group.
problem: From 18 Feb 2027, LMT, EV and industrial batteries over 2 kWh need a passport reachable by QR code and linked to a unique identifier. The Annex XIII list has 71 entries, but 'not every field is due in February 2027': fields are day-one, modelled-now-populated-later, or waiting on secondary legislation. Access-rights rules are slipping to Q4 2026 and key standards are still in draft. Passports must track state of health, cycle counts and status changes after repurposing or remanufacturing. As one guide says, 'a once-published PDF or marketing microsite is not enough'. Enterprise passport platforms are priced for large firms with compliance teams.
solution: Two products. (1) A brand starter package: a field-status mapper that says which of the 71 fields are due now, later or pending; ISO/IEC 15459-style unique ID and QR generation; a hosted passport page; and a written-authorisation template so the brand can legally delegate passport management to us. (2) A free repair-shop and refurbisher app that scans the QR, logs state-of-health tests, cell swaps, cycle data and second-life events, and pushes them into the brand's passport. Shops get a free workflow tool and repair leads. Brands pay for the passport and the event stream. This also lines up with the replaceable-battery rule that applies from 18 Feb 2027 and with the Right to Repair Directive.
why_now: The passport deadline is under 5 months away and the access-rights implementing act is late. Replaceable portable batteries and e-bike batteries become an obligation on the same date. Eighteen Member States had not notified full transposition of the Right to Repair Directive by September 2026, which leaves national repair rules unsettled while shops still have to service batteries.
revenue_model: Brand setup of EUR 2-5k. Subscription of roughly EUR 1-3 per battery per year (or a EUR 300-1,500 per month floor). Optional per-event fee for verified state-of-health tests. Later, a paid API for insurers and second-life buyers.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone sells 'publish a QR page'. The law's real burden is a lifecycle record kept consistent across systems and updated when the battery is serviced or repurposed, and that happens in repair shops that no passport vendor serves. Evidence: 'The hard part is not publishing a page. The hard part is keeping model-level, plant-level, and individual-battery records consistent', passports must track state of health, cycle counts and status changes, and batteries allow the operator to authorise another actor in writing to manage the passport (https://infodpp.eu/en/blog/battery-dpp-deadline-february-2027/). Mid-scale companies are named as the likely pressure point (https://www.batterytechonline.com/design-manufacturing/preparing-for-eu-battery-qr-code-standards-in-2027) and passport software is described as badly priced for small manufacturers (https://dpp-tool.com/en/guide/dpp-software-comparison/). Replaceability and spare-battery availability from 18 Feb 2027 are covered at https://www.intertek.com/blog/2025/06-27-2027-reqs-for-removability-and-replaceability-of-batteries-in-electrical-products/. Right to Repair transposition gap: https://www.eunews.it/en/2026/09/25/right-to-repair-italy-and-17-other-countries-have-failed-to-transpose-the-directive-eu-infringement-proceedings-begin/.
first_30_days: Build a spreadsheet-based field-status mapper for the 71 fields and offer it as a free download. Contact 30 small e-bike brands and pack assemblers found through European trade fairs, cycling industry associations and importer lists. Sell 3 paid 'passport readiness sprint' engagements at EUR 1.5-3k each that end with a hosted pilot passport for one battery model. In parallel, recruit 10 independent e-bike shops to test the scan-and-log app on real service jobs.

title: Vendor Exit Desk for Fleets and Contractors
one_liner: A contingency-fee service that gets small fleets and home-service contractors out of predatory software and telematics contracts, and recovers the money the vendors keep billing.
customer: Owner-operators and fleets of 5-200 trucks locked into telematics or ELD contracts (Samsara, Motive). Also HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors on ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro or Jobber, and small property managers on AppFolio. The owner or office manager pays, and only out of money recovered or saved.
problem: These vendors sell month-to-month or 1-year terms, then enforce hidden multi-year renewals, exit fees, ship-date billing and auto-renew windows. Support is now AI-only, so the customer cannot reach a human who can fix it. One Samsara reviewer was charged $29,000 for a 3-year contract after negotiating 1 year. Another lost about $32,000 paying for unused devices for 1 year and 9 months. ServiceTitan customers report quoted exit fees of $22,000, $29,000 and $37,000. An AppFolio reviewer was billed a $1,290 cancellation fee and said cancelling took 4 months.
solution: The customer forwards the contract and 3 recent invoices. The service does six things. (1) Extract renewal dates and notice windows, then send certified-mail non-renewal notices on the right day. (2) Audit billing against reality: billing that started at ship date rather than install date, decommissioned trucks still billed, duplicate accounts, and charges after cancellation. (3) Build a dispute packet with the sales promises, the timeline, and a card-network chargeback filing where the payment was on a business card. (4) Negotiate with the vendor's retention or legal team, with a partner attorney handling demand letters so the desk does not practice law itself. (5) Handle the data export. (6) Refer the customer to a replacement vendor that pays a bounty for the switch.
why_now: The 1-2 star reviews are dated 2026. They show vendors under public-market pressure enforcing renewals and paywalling features, for example Samsara charging $10 per truck for a feature shown in the demo. They also show support moving to AI. A Housecall Pro review dated Sept 28, 2026 says 'No support unless you want to speak with AI', and a Tithe.ly reviewer says the same in Feb 2026. Customers have nobody to call, so a human escalation path is now something they will pay for.
revenue_model: 25-30% of recovered or avoided dollars, with no fee if nothing is recovered. A $199 flat billing audit for small accounts. A $300-$1,000 referral bounty from the competing vendor that wins each switched fleet or contractor. An optional $29 per vendor per year renewal-watch subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The leads identify themselves. Each reviewer posts the vendor, the dollar amount, the date and the grievance publicly, so the whole first-year pipeline is already listed. Evidence: Samsara ($29,000 3-year contract, $32,000 unused devices, $900/month billed from ship date, $10/truck feature paywall) at https://www.trustpilot.com/review/samsara.com. ServiceTitan ($22K, $29K and $37K exit quotes) at https://www.trustpilot.com/review/servicetitan.com. Motive (renewal-window traps, charged again after cancelling) at https://www.trustpilot.com/review/gomotive.com. AppFolio ($1,290 fee, 4-month cancellation) at https://www.trustpilot.com/review/appfolio.com. Housecall Pro (charged $189 three times after cancelling, price doubled from $351 to $681) at https://www.trustpilot.com/review/housecallpro.com. The winning product is not software. It is a library of each vendor's contract clauses, notice windows and escalation paths, built up case by case, and it gets more effective with every dispute settled.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: pull the roughly 300 public 1-2 star reviews from the last 12 months across those 5 vendors and tag each by vendor, dollar amount and whether the customer is still active. Days 8-14: contact reviewers by the review reply or an email lookup, offering a free contract read. Sign a contract attorney on a small retainer. Days 15-30: take 5-10 contingency cases and publish 'how to cancel [vendor]' pages, since people search that phrase. Use the settled cases to build the clause library. Also pitch 2 competing telematics vendors on the switch bounty.

title: Offline Brain for Talking Toys
one_liner: A sub-$20 on-device speech-and-language module that lets toys hold child-safe conversations with no cloud, no audio leaving the toy and parent-readable summaries on the parent's phone.
customer: Toy brands and ODMs, indie AI-toy startups and kids' IP licensors who fear cloud data liability.
problem: Cloud-based AI toys stream children's voices to servers, which the amended COPPA rule (biometrics, retention limits, separate opt-in for third-party sharing) makes risky. Brand exposure is rising after consumer tests and lawsuits. Toy makers lack model-safety teams, and per-conversation cloud costs collide with a one-time hardware sale.
solution: A reference design and software stack: kid-tuned speech recognition, a 1-4B-parameter model fine-tuned for age-banded personas and refusals, and text-to-speech on a $10-15 NPU chip. Safety-locked story and play modes, and Bluetooth summaries to a parent app. Licensed to ODMs, with dev kits for startups.
why_now: Small on-device models reached conversational quality in 2025-26 and cheap NPUs run them in real time, so the technology only just became feasible. Regulation turns cloud audio into a liability, and holiday 2026 is the first big AI-toy season.
revenue_model: $2-4 per unit licence, $299 dev kits, and paid NRE for custom personas.
non_obvious_insight: The cloud is both the risk and the cost. On-device removes marginal cost and turns COPPA from a burden into a marketing claim ('nothing leaves the toy'), fixing the broken subscription-for-hardware model.
first_30_days: Prototype on a Raspberry Pi 5 or RK3588 board with an off-the-shelf small model. Measure latency and accuracy on consented child speech. Demo to 15 indie toy makers on Kickstarter and Crowd Supply and to 2 ODMs. Aim for 2 paid dev-kit pilots with $5k NRE each.

title: Pre-Dawn Childcare Pods for Construction Crews
one_liner: Contractors buy reserved 5:00am-4:00pm childcare slots near job sites from licensed home providers, so crews can start at 6am without losing parents.
customer: General contractors and specialty subs (electrical, framing, concrete), especially on data-center and big subdivision projects, plus local homebuilder associations and apprenticeship funds. The 45F credit lets them recover 40-50% of the cost.
problem: Crews start at 5:30-7am and often work 10-12 hour days, but licensed care opens at 6:30-7am. ICE enforcement, retirements and data-center overtime are already draining the workforce, and construction is only about 4% women. Providers cannot staff 5am hours without guaranteed revenue. Childcare workers earn about $33K, so nobody can afford premium-hour pay.
solution: Contract with licensed family providers and small centers near job sites and staging areas to run early-hours pods with reserved capacity on a monthly retainer. Cap care at a safe number of hours (about 10) and design for early-arrival sleep. The platform handles enrollment, insurance, shift scheduling, drop-off logistics and 45F paperwork. For megasites with thousands of workers, add factory-built child-care modules on site.
why_now: The 45F credit rose to 40% (50% for small businesses) from 2026 and reportedly allows third-party and pooled arrangements, so a group of subs can share one program. ABC says construction must add 349K workers in 2026, immigrant workers are over 25% of the workforce and are being pulled off sites, and data centers are absorbing about a third of the shortage. Retention is the acute buyer pain.
revenue_model: $350-600 per reserved slot per month paid by contractors, 12-15% platform fee on top of provider pay, and tax-credit advisory fees.
non_obvious_insight: The people who cannot use standard 7-6 childcare are the only buyers who will pay a premium, and construction employers already pay per-diems, housing and overtime to keep skilled hands. Replacing one journeyman costs thousands, so a few hundred dollars a month for a reliable slot is cheap. A retainer is what unlocks provider supply for the early hours.
first_30_days: Choose one metro with a data-center or subdivision surge. Interview 10 subs' HR or safety directors and survey crews on childcare needs. Sign two family providers willing to open at 5am for guaranteed pay. Sell a pilot of 10 reserved slots to one mid-size electrical or framing contractor, then get a CPA to sign off on the 45F treatment.

title: Task-Shifting Engine for Tech-Led Vet Visits
one_liner: Standing-order templates, scheduling and a state-by-state supervision rules database that let clinics move routine care from vets to technicians and, soon, VPAs, without breaking practice acts.
customer: Independent clinics adopting a team-based model, multi-state clinic groups, and VPA-employing practices. Later: PIMS and telehealth vendors licensing the rules API.
problem: Vet supply is nearly flat (91,100 vets; about 3,100 openings a year) while techs are scarce (about 2 per vet versus a 4:1 ideal, with most leaving within 4 years). The team-based model is how affordable clinics reach invoices about 44% below average, yet PIMS scheduling is built around doctor visits. Nobody supplies compliant protocols for who may do what under which supervision in each state.
solution: A library of 'tech appointment' types (booster vaccines, rechecks, suture removal, senior lab draws, weight programs, dental prep) with standing orders, consent scripts and a DVM sign-off queue. A versioned rules database maps each task to state supervision levels, with alerts when boards change rules, and audit logs show who did what under whose supervision. A scheduling plug-in books the right role and length.
why_now: Colorado State is launching an MS for the new VPA license (dogs and cats, supervised, routine surgery and tests), and it has been more than a decade in the making. Roll-ups now span many states, and clinics need to raise output per DVM. AI scribes and agents are generating plans that implicitly delegate tasks.
revenue_model: $199-399 per clinic per month for templates and scheduling; $500-5K per month for rules API and multi-state groups; VPA program design consulting.
non_obvious_insight: A new professional tier shifts value to whoever holds the rules and the protocols. In human health, scope-of-practice changes (NPs, PAs) spawned decades of compliance and protocol software. Vet medicine is at the start of that curve, and the rules database is the moat while templates are the wedge.
first_30_days: With a vet-law attorney, build a matrix of 10 states by about 40 tasks from statutes and board rules. Publish a free 'Can my tech do this?' checker in vet-tech communities. Pilot the appointment templates in 5 clinics and aim to sell 3 multi-state groups on the rules feed.

title: Positive Pay for Stablecoin Wallets
one_liner: Give mid-market finance teams the control environment auditors will demand before approving stablecoin flows: vendor wallet verification, sanctions and taint screening, and freeze-risk checks.
customer: Finance teams at $20M-$500M revenue companies starting to pay and receive USDC or USDT (via Citi and Coinbase, Stripe/Bridge or Circle), and the CPA and fractional-CFO firms that serve them.
problem: Stablecoin payments are irreversible, and wallet-address swaps and address poisoning are the new business email compromise. Companies inherit sanctions exposure (Senate Democrats allege about $2B of Iranian flows through Tether in a year). Funds received from a tainted wallet can be frozen. There is no bank-style 'positive pay' equivalent.
solution: Vendor wallet verification via signed challenge and callback, allowlist enforcement in the payment approval flow (Slack and email approvals), pre-payment counterparty screening, post-receipt taint checks, and NetSuite/QuickBooks reconciliation at the invoice level. Continuous behavioral KYC scoring, the gap flagged by The Block, is the roadmap.
why_now: Citi and Coinbase launched stablecoin acceptance with fiat settlement on 2026-09-28. Annual stablecoin volume tops $90T and doubled year on year, daily turnover is 0.78x, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
revenue_model: $500-$3,000 per month SaaS plus per-screen fees, sold through CPA and fractional-CFO channel partners.
non_obvious_insight: Corporate adoption is gated by the controller's control environment, not by wallets. Positive Pay is a large business in traditional banking, and the wallet analog doesn't exist. Whoever ships the audit-ready control set becomes the default checklist.
first_30_days: Interview 25 controllers and CFOs with live or planned stablecoin flows. Ship a browser extension plus Slack approvals for wallet verification and allowlists. Sell $299 per month pilots through five CPA firms serving importers and crypto-adjacent SMEs.

title: Finishing Milk Run for Small Machine Shops
one_liner: A scheduled truck route and capacity-slot exchange that pools small lots from many shops into full tank loads and racks at platers, anodizers, heat treaters and powder coaters.
customer: Job shops and small OEM plants (5-150 employees) that machine or fabricate parts but outsource plating, anodize, passivation, heat treat, e-coat or powder coat. The buyer is the shop owner or plant manager. The second customer is the finisher, who gets fuller tanks and lines.
problem: Everyone talks about a shortage of machinists, but the real reshoring bottleneck is finishing. Parts wait 9-15 days for a truck and for enough volume to fill a tank or rack. Finishers apply minimum-charge lots that punish small runs. Shops drive parts themselves or pay LTL rates of $150-$300 per pallet, and a batch's lead time is mostly waiting, not processing. The 2026 Reshoring Initiative data show finishing capacity as part of the bottleneck, and permits make new capacity slow and rare.
solution: Run daily box-truck routes around a dense corridor (Akron-Canton-Cleveland-Youngstown) with QR-coded totes and text-message status. Pre-buy weekly capacity slots at 8-12 vetted finishers, pool many shops' small lots into shared racks, and guarantee 3-5 day door-to-door turnaround. Route data and slot utilisation decide which finisher gets which parts. Expand to a second corridor (Columbus-Dayton-Cincinnati) once route density works.
why_now: Reshoring is adding machined and fabricated volume in the US while environmental permits have made new plating, anodize and coating lines almost impossible to build. Existing finishers are running full but inefficiently. Lightweight route and tote software plus cheap dispatch tools remove the reason this stayed a hand-arranged, phone-call business.
revenue_model: $55-$95 per stop or tote pickup, an 8-12% margin on capacity-slot resale, and a $299/month booking and tracking subscription. Roughly 40 active shops on one corridor gets to $1M ARR. Later, purchase or co-develop a permitted finishing line inside a 'factory condo'.
non_obvious_insight: An anodize or zinc cycle takes hours. Most of the lead time is a batch waiting for a truck and waiting for enough peers to fill a rack. That is a logistics-and-pooling problem hiding inside what everyone treats as a process-capacity problem, and it is solvable without building a single tank.
first_30_days: Lease one box truck or contract a local courier per stop. Interview 15 shops and 4 finishers. Launch one route on Tuesdays and Thursdays with 8 pilot shops at $65 per stop. Get two finishers to guarantee 48-hour processing for pooled lots in exchange for weekly committed volume. Track everything in Airtable with printed QR tags and text updates, and publish on-time-in-full data after 6 weeks.

title: Unwind Desk for California's 3-Day Car Return
one_liner: A per-return concierge that unwinds a cancelled used-car deal (lender, add-on administrators, DMV, sales tax, commissions) inside California's new 48-hour refund deadline. It then turns the return data into a return-risk pool.
customer: California used-car dealers, especially independents and BHPH lots that sell 30 to 200 used cars a month and have no back-office bench. They pay $195 to $250 per return, or a standby retainer. Later, insurers and MGAs buy the underwriting data.
problem: From Oct 1, 2026, SB 766 gives buyers a 3-day right to cancel a used vehicle priced at $50,000 or less. Within 48 hours of cancellation the dealer must cancel the contract and refund the buyer, less only the deductions the law allows for mileage and damage. That is easy to write and very hard to do. The cost of an unwind is the cascade, not the car. The dealer has to reach the lender that has funded or is holding the contract, cancel each service contract and GAP with its administrator, and charge back the F&I commission. It also has to reverse the title, registration and sales tax, refund the down payment and any trade, and document the vehicle condition to justify any deduction. Independents have never done this at volume, and one botched unwind creates a refund violation and a private-plaintiff claim.
solution: Unwind-as-a-service. The dealer forwards the cancellation notice. The desk runs a checklist workflow that notifies the lender, submits cancellations to administrators with the correct pro-rata or full-refund basis, prepares the DMV and tax reversals, calculates the refund and permitted deductions, and produces a compliance file that meets the two-year retention rule. A delivery-day photo and video capture link is bundled, because permitted deductions depend on condition documentation. After 6 months of volume, the desk holds the only dataset on return rates, timing and loss per return in a mandatory-return regime. That data is enough to price a per-unit return-risk cover (roughly $60 to $120 per used unit) through a licensed MGA or insurer partner.
why_now: The law takes effect Oct 1, 2026, so the first returns arrive within days. No US state has had a mandatory 3-day return on used cars at this scale. The 2025 to 2026 run of subprime stress, roughly 30% of trade-ins underwater and repossessions at about 3M a year, means many buyers will discover mid-week that they can't afford the payment. That is the buyer most likely to use the cancellation right.
revenue_model: Flat fee per processed return ($195 to $250). Standby retainer of about $99 per month per store for priority handling. Phase 2: 10 to 20% of premium as an MGA on the return-risk pool. Phase 3: license the cancellation-cascade workflow to DMS and eContract vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody knows the real return rate. Everyone models it on Carvana's 7-day return, but the buyers who return are not typical, because the F&I office sees payment shock and buyer's remorse first. A 48-hour refund deadline is shorter than the time a lender, administrator or DMV normally takes to process anything, so the dealer's exposure is process failure, not vehicle depreciation. Whoever owns the process owns the data, and the data is what makes the insurance product priceable.
first_30_days: Write the cascade checklist by state and by lender for the 20 most common California indirect lenders and 15 administrators. Approach the California Independent Automobile Dealers Association and 10 high-volume independents. Sell a $99 per month standby plan with a guaranteed 24-hour turnaround per return. Handle the first 20 returns manually with a shared spreadsheet and e-sign before writing any software. Log every step's time and dollar cost, since that log becomes the actuarial dataset.

title: Guardrail Gateway for Law-Firm AI Agents
one_liner: A policy proxy between AI agents and practice-management, billing and trust-accounting systems that enforces ethics rules (trust funds, conflicts, confidentiality) and logs every action for the bar and the insurer.
customer: Solo and small firms (5 or fewer attorneys), the exact segment adopting MCP connectors. Distribution partners are practice-management vendors and malpractice carriers that want to underwrite agent use.
problem: 8am's MyCase MCP connector exposes 73 actions across cases, billing and intake, and 60+ firms adopted it in month one. An agent that can write to billing and trust ledgers can commingle funds, send a privileged detail to the wrong client or email a client without review. Those are disciplinary and malpractice events that no hallucination checker prevents, and solo lawyers have no IT staff, policy or audit trail.
solution: An MCP gateway between Claude, ChatGPT or a 'Firm Agent' and Clio, MyCase and LawPay. Rules block any write touching the trust account without attorney approval by SMS, enforce ethical walls between matters, redact privileged content going to non-approved models, hold outbound client communications for review and rate-limit actions. Every call goes into a tamper-evident log, and a monthly 'agent audit' PDF answers the insurer questionnaire.
why_now: 8am launched its MCP integration in Sep 2026 and says nearly all of its new Firm Agent features already work via MCP, so law-practice data is flowing to third-party agents for the first time. ABA Formal Opinion 512 (2024) on generative-AI ethics gives the duties a written source (background, verify).
revenue_model: $79-199/firm/month, carrier-sponsored programs at $10-20 per insured firm per month, and white-label licensing to practice-management vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The risk from agents is authority (moving money and information), not wrong words. Legal ethics rules are crisp about authority (trust accounting, confidentiality, conflicts), so they compile into policy, unlike 'accuracy'. Distribution will run through practice-management marketplaces, not law-firm websites.
first_30_days: Build the gateway for one platform (Clio or MyCase MCP) with six rules. Recruit 10 small firms through user groups and run it free as a 30-day 'agent audit' that shows near-misses, then convert at $99/month. Take the audit output to two state-bar-affiliated malpractice carriers.

title: Stablecoin Cash-Out Float for Corner Shops
one_liner: Stablecoins made sending money nearly free, so the scarce thing is cash at the last mile, and the margin goes to whoever finances the agents.
customer: Pharmacies, tiendas and kiosks that act as cash-out agents in Colombia, Mexico, Argentina and Nigeria, plus the stablecoin remittance and wallet apps that need them.
problem: A $200 US-to-Colombia transfer costs $12.13 on legacy rails versus about $0.01 in stablecoins, but recipients still want local cash. Small agents run out of float and refuse large withdrawals.
solution: A float-management app that shows each agent's cash position, advances intraday float against next-day USDC settlement and routes recipients to agents with liquidity. The wedge is 100 pharmacies on one remittance corridor for a single anchor partner.
why_now: Nigeria opened a stablecoin sandbox (Aug 12) and Kenya passed digital-currency legislation (Aug 6). Yellow Card is hiring in LatAm and SEA, and Felix has processed $8B over WhatsApp.
revenue_model: A 1-1.5% spread on float turnover plus a per-payout fee from the remitter.
non_obvious_insight: As stablecoin transfer fees go to zero, the margin migrates to the last ten metres of physical cash. This is cash logistics dressed up as fintech.
first_30_days: Sign one wallet or remittance partner as anchor and raise a roughly $50k float line from a debt fund. Onboard 20 pharmacies in one city.

title: Break-Glass Interim Operators for Deceased Owners' Businesses
one_liner: An on-call bench of laid-off COOs and ops directors who step in within 48 hours when the sole owner of a small business dies, keeping it alive until the heirs can sell or close it.
customer: Estate attorneys, CPAs, SBA lenders and key-person insurers who need the business to keep its value, plus the widow or heirs. The estate ultimately pays from business cash flow or sale proceeds. Target businesses: HVAC and trades firms, machine shops, independent insurance agencies, restaurants and other 5-50 employee owner-dependent companies.
problem: Probate treats assets as inert (houses, accounts), but a running business melts within 90 days when the owner dies: bank signing authority, payroll, licenses, customer relationships and key employees all hinge on one person. Executors are grieving family. Attorneys cannot run a company. Brokers cannot sell one in freefall. Boomers still own a large share of employer businesses, so this is a huge, mostly invisible transfer.
solution: A vetted bench of interim managers with a 72-hour playbook: secure bank and payroll access via letters testamentary or a special administrator, notify customers and vendors, fund key-employee retention from the estate, arrange licensing 'qualifier' coverage where required, stabilize for 60-90 days, prep a data room, then hand off to a broker or buyer. AI tools (contract abstraction, bookkeeping analysis, KPI dashboards) let a newcomer understand the business in about a week. Owners can pre-buy a 'continuity plan' retainer.
why_now: The largest generational transfer of small businesses is under way (Cerulli: $124T through 2048, about 81% from Boomers and older), while the 2026 labor market is full of experienced ops leaders who cannot find roles. Cheap AI document and finance tooling makes fast onboarding of an unfamiliar business feasible for the first time.
revenue_model: Interim GM day rate of $900-1,500 billed to the estate, with the bench member keeping about 65%. Pre-need continuity retainer of about $1,200/yr for solo owners. Success fee on a sale, in coordination with brokers.
non_obvious_insight: The estate needs a verb, not a noun. The legal system has a process for distributing what a person owned but none for continuing what a person did. Unemployed senior operators are the perfect supply for that verb, and their downside is only the awkwardness of arriving during grief.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 laid-off ops and finance leaders. Write the 72-hour playbook. Offer a free 'owner-death readiness check' at bar association and CPA society events for 30 attorneys and accountants. Sell a $1,200/yr continuity retainer to 20 solo-owner businesses through one insurance agency or SBA lender's client list. The first at-need engagements will come from those attorneys' existing clients.

title: Motor-Rewind Shops Become Drone-Motor Cells
one_liner: Qualify a network of existing U.S. electric-motor repair shops to wind and test compliant drone motors with non-Chinese magnets for Drone Dominance suppliers.
customer: Attritable-drone makers and tier-1 subsystem suppliers, including Gauntlet participants and Blue UAS suppliers. They pay per motor (about $60-150, my estimate, versus about $15-30 imported).
problem: The Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program targets more than 200,000 drones by 2027, and about 60,000 are to be ordered from Gauntlet 2 winners. At four motors per quadcopter that is about 240,000 motors for one tranche. China holds about 94% of magnet manufacturing, heavy rare earths stay tight through 2027, and capital is chasing airframes and software, not motors.
solution: Recruit motor-repair shops that already own winding skill, varnish and potting ovens, balancing and hipot test benches. Standardize a 'motor cell kit' (needle winders and fixtures, a single test spec, lot traceability logging) on a lease. The network operator holds customer contracts, source-verified magnet, bearing and lamination supply from domestic vendors, quality paperwork and DPAS-rated order handling, and passes work down. Each shop is audited like a franchisee.
why_now: Gauntlet cadence (roughly every six months) turns motors into a recurring bottleneck, and export controls make compliant sourcing urgent. Motor repair is a slow-shrinking industry, so shops have idle capacity. The Navy is retreating from early-stage funding, so distributed capacity without venture capital is the workable route.
revenue_model: 15-25% operator margin on motor sales, a $15-30k onboarding and equipment-lease fee per shop, and certification renewals. Later expand to ESCs, gimbals and wire harnesses using the same shop network.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is winding know-how and test discipline, not CNC capacity. Motor repair shops are typically classified as repair, so industrial-base maps built from manufacturing codes miss over a thousand of them. Hidden capacity, not new plants, is the fastest path to supply.
first_30_days: Contact regional chapters of the electrical apparatus service association to recruit 5 shops. Get 3 drone makers that currently fly Chinese motors to specify a compliant second-source design. Sell a prototype lot of about 500 motors with customer prepayment and run a first-article test.
